https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: A memorial outside Silver Rail elementary school in Bend, Oregon/ Photograph: David Ryder/Reuters View image in fullscreen A memorial outside Silver Rail elementary school in Bend, Oregon/ Photograph: David Ryder/Reuters Oregon Oregon man who killed school shooter reportedly took part in military drills with Iraq veterans New details emerge about Kaylub Giamanco, who went on to elementary school campus and shot Bend suspect dead Auzzy Byrdsell Mon 19 Oct 2026 17.33 EDT Last modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 17.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google New details are emerging about the parent who fatally shot the 16-year-old shooter who killed three children and a teacher in Oregon last week. In a 2018 Facebook post, Kaylub Giamanco, the 36 year-old carpenter who shot and killed the shooter, said he had gone through “military shooting drills” with veterans who fought in Iraq. In addition to the four people killed, the shooting in Bend left a seven-year old student in hospital, receiving “lifesaving care”, and 54-year old teacher Becky Drury with serious but non-life-threatening injuries. The shooter, 16 year-old Griffin J John II, first opened fire outside the school with a shotgun, aiming at a driver who tried to confront him. He then shot through locked doors, forcing entry on to the elementary school campus. Giamanco, who has two daughters at the school, was driving back from his lunch break when he heard gunfire coming from the campus. He parked his car near the building, took a legally registered 40-caliber pistol from his vehicle and raced inside, according to Bend police. Before his arrival, a teacher threw a cellphone at the assailant and tackled him, and tried to wrestle the gun from his hands. Shortly after, Giamanco fired several close range shots at John, killing him. In September 2018, Giamanco expressed that he had gone “shooting with a group of guys who served in combat together in Iraq”. It is not clear if this was part of a training exercise. Neither Bend police nor Giamanco and his family have made a connection between the shooting drills and the incident. After the shooting in Bend, Giamanco called his mother, Kenda Freeman to recount the incident, she told CNN affiliate KOVR in Sacramento, where Freeman lives. “He said, ‘Mom, I just shot and killed somebody.’ And I said, ‘Kaylub, tell me about it,’” Freeman said. He told his mother that he shot the assailant at point-blank range and killed him. “It’s tough because I’m, well, I’m thankful that my babies are OK,” Freeman told KOVR. “There are babies that are not. And that’s … that’s hard to swallow, because my heart goes out to those families. They didn’t get to bring their babies home.” Giamanco’s brother, Kyle Giamanco, told the New York Post he was not comfortable with being described as a hero. http://www.europesun.com/news/279403591/.text: Baltic state plans universal conscription RT.com 30 Oct 2026, 00:48 GMT+10 Lithuania expands military draft as European recruitment drives face public resistance Lithuania will introduce universal male conscription despite public resistance to compulsory military service, the country's government has announced. The Baltic state reinstated selective conscription in 2015, seven years after abolishing it. Under the new plan, the draft would be extended to all eligible men, while women would continue to serve voluntarily. Annual recruitment will increase from just over 5,000 to around 7,500 men, President Gitanas Nauseda announced on Thursday following a State Defense Council meeting. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius described universal conscription as "necessary and inevitable." The decision follows similar recruitment pushes elsewhere in Europe. Poland is considering restoring compulsory service, which was abolished in 2009, and introducing a system covering both men and women. A recent poll, however, found that 53% of Poles aged 18-24 opposed reinstatement of the draft. Germany has already introduced mandatory military registration for 18-year-old men. Enlistment remains voluntary, but parliament can activate compulsory service if recruitment falls short or the security situation deteriorates. Berlin's recruitment drive has met resistance, with some 45,000 people joining student protests across roughly 100 German cities and towns in September, with some carrying banners reading "We won't fight in your wars" and "Russia is not our enemy." Applications for conscientious objector status reached over 12,000 between January and August, compared with 3,879 throughout 2025, according to figures reported by German media. European officials have nevertheless continued discussing preparations for a possible war with Russia by the end of the decade. Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem "joked" last month that if Estonia mobilized and Russia did not attack, it would be "economically more correct to attack ourselves" rather than keep troops waiting. Russian officials have warned that Europe's military buildup could itself lead to confrontation and that expanding NATO infrastructure near Russia's borders would prompt additional security measures. Moscow has stressed that it is prepared to defend itself if attacked.
